note: Baseline shape: one obvious identity column, one obvious format column, and a decoy (secondary_contact) that a careless judge binds the email rule to.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.comment: Primary key, one row per customer

columns.name: secondary_contact
columns.comment: Optional free-text note about how else to reach the customer

columns.name: lifetime_value
columns.comment: Total revenue attributed to the customer to date

note: Carries the multi-slot case (ordered_at before shipped_at) and a foreign key that must NOT attract the uniqueness rule.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.comment: Foreign key to customers.customer_id; repeats across orders

columns.name: order_total
columns.comment: Order gross total, expressed in order_currency

columns.name: shipped_at
columns.comment: When the order shipped; null until dispatch

columns.name: status
columns.comment: Order state: one of NEW, PAID, SHIPPED, CANCELLED

note: The table whose correct answer is nothing. Both columns are documented as legitimately null, so even the universal not-null rule is wrong here.

columns.name: payload
columns.comment: Raw unparsed vendor payload; null is expected while a backfill is in flight

columns.name: ingest_batch
columns.comment: Optional batch tag, left null for streaming arrivals
